title: FLV video import to library: File > Import > Import Video... wires FLV files into VideoItem library assets
description:
The SWF compiler (task 0757) now fully encodes `VideoItem` library entries as `DefineVideoStream` + per-frame `VideoFrame` tags including FLV demuxing. However, there is no way for the user to get a video into the library — no import UI exists.

The bitmap and sound import flows in `useFileActions.ts` (`importToLibrary`, `importSoundToLibrary`) serve as the template. Video needs the same treatment.

## What to implement

### 1. `importVideoToLibrary()` in `useFileActions.ts`
- Open a native file dialog (Tauri) or `<input type="file">` (browser) filtered to `.flv` files
- Read the file bytes, convert to a base64 data URI (`data:video/x-flv;base64,...`)
- Probe the FLV header to extract `frameCount`, `frameRate`, `width`, `height` (use the existing `demuxFlv` function in `packages/swf/src/video.ts` or parse the FLV header directly)
- Create and return a `VideoItem` using `createVideo()` from `@flash/core` (add this factory to `packages/core/src/model/library.ts` alongside `createBitmap` and `createSound`)

### 2. Wire into `Shell.tsx`
- Call `importVideoToLibrary()` from a `handleImportVideo` callback
- Add the item to the library via `pushDoc(withLibrary(...))`

### 3. Wire into `MenuBar.tsx`
- Add `File > Import > Import Video...` menu item below `Import Sound...`
- Add an `onImportVideo?: () => void` prop to `MenuBarProps` and `MenuBar`

### 4. `createVideo()` factory in `@flash/core`
- Add `createVideo(name, opts?)` alongside `createBitmap`/`createSound` in `model/library.ts`
- Export from `packages/core/src/index.ts`

## Notes
- `VideoItem` is already defined in `packages/core/src/model/types.ts` with fields: `id, name, itemType:"video", dataUri, frameCount, frameRate, width, height`
- `VideoItem` is NOT placeable on stage (see `libraryplace.ts:142`); it renders as a library-only asset that the SWF compiler picks up automatically
- `demuxFlv` is in `packages/swf/src/video.ts`; import it in `useFileActions.ts` or expose a thin probe helper from `@flash/swf`

## Acceptance
1. File > Import > Import Video... opens a file picker filtered to `.flv`
2. Selecting a valid FLV creates a `VideoItem` entry in the Library panel
3. Publishing the document produces a SWF that contains `DefineVideoStream` + `VideoFrame` tags for the video
4. Works in both Tauri (native dialog) and browser (`<input type="file">`) modes
